job: Flipping the harness default profile so a fresh install denies tool calls, outbound network, and MCP credentials unless an operator explicitly grants them
outcome: A tagged stable release whose changelog states capability, network, and MCP-credential gating are enabled by default on a clean install
motivation: Hardening landed piecemeal in 2026.6.x while gating stayed opt-in, leaving fresh installs exposed to the documented injection risk

task.who: the harness project's core security maintainers and release owners
task.what: Make least-privilege the shipped default execution profile
task.where: The harness default config and stable release branch
task.when: From the June 2026.6.x patches through Q4 2026
task.why: Opt-in gating leaves clean installs unprotected by default
task.how: Default-deny config flip plus changelog and docs update

job: Publishing the converging evidence that ties agent risk categories to CVEs and proves no agent config resists prompt injection, forcing defense to the harness layer
outcome: Authoritative reports and benchmark scores that make least-privilege defaults the expected baseline for coding-agent harnesses
motivation: If the model layer cannot resist injection, the harness layer must carry the defense, and that case must be made publicly

task.who: OWASP agentic working group and StakeBench benchmark researchers
task.what: Publish CVE-linked risk rankings and injection-resistance scores
task.where: OWASP 2026 agentic report and StakeBench results
task.when: Through 2026 ahead of the Q4 release window
task.why: Evidence pressures maintainers to ship gating as default
task.how: Indirect and direct prompt-injection test suites against agent configs

job: Shipping stricter network-policy and MCP-credential-filtering defaults around their sandbox so a competing harness lands default gating first
outcome: A same-direction release that defaults to network and credential gating, validating least-privilege-by-default across the harness category
motivation: Being first to ship default least-privilege wins security credibility against the presumed first mover in a converging field

task.who: NemoClaw and Hermes Agent harness engineering teams
task.what: Default-enable network policy and MCP credential filtering
task.where: OpenShell and Tirith pre-execution sandbox layers
task.why: Shipping default gating first earns security leadership
